That wakeup was the fallback timer I set before the tuning run finished. Run `beoqtxqz6` has already completed and I used its results, so nothing new came in.

Its best parameters scored 0.0846 on the seeds it was tuned on (from 0.0939), but showed no gain on the separate 80-seed check (0.1007 → 0.1026). I kept those parameters only because, combined with starting the simulated endgame at item 4940 instead of 4920, they did best on two untouched 80-seed sets (0.0907 and 0.0909).

**Where things stand:** `solution.py` scores **0.1596** on dev with the official evaluator (best previous attempt: 0.658), and the full run takes about 1.4s of the 60s allowed.

I'm stopping here. The remaining gap is about 1.5–2 extra bins per instance, and none of my last variants beat the noise: more simulation samples, starting the simulated endgame earlier, fading the penalties near the end, or wider parameter searches. On dev, one bin on one instance moves the score by 0.01, so further tuning against dev would just be fitting noise.
